blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Serpentine

items.t: ALR frame for the feed's acreage ground (the rule book that actually governs most of this ground): the visible cards are dominated by farm and acreage parcels. On ALR parcels the ALC housing frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), with any secondary suite inside the principal residence, and subdivision of ALR land requires Agricultural Land Commission permission outside limited regulation exceptions — depositing a strata plan is a subdivision (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; ALCA s. 21(1)), so ALR ground cannot be stratified without ALC permission. Which feed parcels are actually in the ALR: UNVERIFIED — check parcel by parcel on ALC mapping; listing text is not an ALR determination.

Form B (for strata stock generally — this ground has none verified): Strata Property Act s. 59 — on a resale purchase the strata must provide a Form B Information Certificate stating strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and a summary of the strata's insurance, with rules, budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. It has no application to a freehold acreage parcel.

Depreciation reports and CRF (strata stock generally): since July 1, 2024, stratas with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, no deferral by vote; and since November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the operating fund to the CRF. Neither rule creates strata stock on this ground.

Short-term rentals (Surrey): under 90 consecutive days per patron; only the owner may host, the owner must live at the property as their primary residence, tenants cannot run one, and a business licence at $358 per year is required. On ALR parcels the ALC short-term accommodation limits in the first bullet govern instead.

items.t: Fee-simple lots and acreages are the form: the twelve visible feed cards are acreage-led — estate houses on 9–12 acres, working blueberry farms to 57 acres (including a 48.28-acre parcel and a 21.46-acre farm, in listing text), vacant land parcels (including a court-ordered-sale lot on 176 Street, in listing text), and two roughly 1-acre Campbell Heights parcels described in their listing text as development/industrial-side opportunities. Individual card prices are feed data that change; none is frozen here as a market fact, and no listing address or asking price beyond the feed's own street-level showing is carried. Unless title says otherwise these are fee-simple purchases: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees. A strata-versus-freehold split for this ground is UNVERIFIED — no official source publishes one.
Bare-land strata — none verified on this ground

ALR vs non-ALR split: no split is published and none is stated. The visible cards are dominated by farm and acreage parcels in listing text, but which feed parcels are actually in the Agricultural Land Reserve is UNVERIFIED — check parcel by parcel on ALC mapping; listing text is not an ALR determination.

Serviced vs unserviced ground, as the sources state it: feed cards variously claim city water, wells, irrigation/ditch water and services "at lot line" in listing text — none of that is verified here, and on farm ground the servicing answer drives value more than the house does. Servicing for any specific parcel is confirmed with the City and on the ground, parcel by parcel.

Court-order, preload and approval claims, documented AS listing text, never as inventory or fact: one visible card is a court-ordered sale with a stated court date and accepted price, and others claim preload pads and approvals — confirm each against court and City records before relying on it.

Assemblies / development sites, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: none is documented as a proposal in this area's research. The Campbell Heights parcels' "development/industrial-side opportunity" language is listing marketing text, carried above as exactly that — it is not a documented assembly, rezoning or development proposal, and no proposal is named or counted.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Serpentine?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Serpentine?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Serpentine?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Is Serpentine in Cloverdale or South Surrey?
faq.a: Confirm which ground a specific listing sits on from its address, not from the sub-area label.

faq.q: What PTT should I budget on this ground?
faq.a: On the worked example in — inputs: $1,212,500 fair market value (the community detached median, illustration only), fully residential, no exemption — the bill is $22,250. Farm and mixed-use parcels can split portions; have a lawyer or notary model the exact bill.

faq.q: Are there any townhouse complexes in Serpentine?
faq.a: The feed's stock is acreage and farm parcels, not named strata complexes, and no named townhouse complex was confirmed on a developer or strata source for this ground.

faq.q: Could a townhouse project be built on a Serpentine farm parcel?
faq.a: Not while the parcel is in the ALR — ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; Strata Property Act s.239), and subdivision itself needs ALC permission.

faq.q: What does the Form B tell me if my search leads me to a strata townhouse nearby?
faq.a: The monthly strata fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the CRF balance, insurance, rules, budget and financial statement, any Rental Disclosure Statement, and the depreciation report attached — within seven days of request, fee capped at $35 plus up to 25 cents per page (Strata Property Act, s. 59

faq.q: How much property transfer tax would I pay on a $900,000 acreage purchase?
faq.a: $16,000 with no exemption — 1% on the first $200,000 plus 2% on the remaining $700,000 (BC Government, PTT: Farm-class and other parcel-specific positions are a title-and-assessment check, not a page figure.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot or farm parcel here?
faq.a: Each one is checked on its own: ALR status on ALC mapping, zone and designation in the City's mapping, and servicing on documents, not listing text.

faq.q: Can I trust a card's "city water," "preload" or "court-ordered" wording?
faq.a: No — servicing, preload/approval and court-order claims on this feed are listing text. Confirm servicing with the City and on the ground, approvals against City records, and any court-ordered sale against court records; Surrey has no Supreme Court registry, so that mapping is UNVERIFIED here.
